stories.title: Effect of Adding Dexamethasone to Bupivacaine in Ultrasound Guided Adductor Canal Block for Post-Operative Analgesia Following Knee Arthroscopy.
stories.description: The article presents findings from multiple clinical trials conducted at Ain Shams University Hospitals in 2023, focusing on anesthesia and critical care interventions. One study compared quadratus lumborum block and erector spinae block for postoperative analgesia in laparoscopic cholecystectomy, finding no significant differences in pain scores, analgesic consumption, mobilization time, or side effects. Another trial evaluated total parenteral nutrition (TPN) versus enteral nutrition (EN) in mechanically ventilated septic patients, reporting similar clinical outcomes but more digestive complications with early EN. A third study demonstrated that adding dexamethasone to bupivacaine in ultrasound-guided adductor canal block significantly prolonged postoperative analgesia and reduced opioid use after knee arthroscopy. These studies contribute to understanding pain management and nutritional support strategies in surgical and critical care settings.

stories.title: Identification and preliminary validation of key exosome-related genes in nasopharyngeal carcinoma through integrative bioinformatics and experimental approaches
stories.description: Exosomes have emerged as significant contributors to the progression of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). However, the characterization of exosome-related gene (ERG) signatures and their immunological relevance in NPC remains limited. This study systematically identified and validated key ERGs in NPC through integrative bioinformatics and machine-learning approaches. Datasets GSE12452 and GSE53819, in addition to known ERGs, were obtained from public databases. Identification of key ERGs employed machine learning, expression verification, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), immune infiltration analysis, in silico compound-target prediction, and molecular docking were also conducted. The expression of key genes underwent experimental validation in clinical NPC tissue samples. A total of 11 candidate genes emerged from machine learning analysis. Of these, LDHA, PIGR, and POSTN demonstrated significant differential expression and passed ROC curve evaluation in both GSE12452 and GSE53819. GSEA revealed involvement of these genes in pathways related to cell cycle checkpoints and DNA replication. Immune infiltration analysis indicated a significantly lower proportion of neutrophils in NPC samples compared to controls, alongside an increased proportion of type 2 helper T cells. Correlation analysis showed that LDHA and POSTN were negatively correlated with neutrophils, while PIGR displayed a positive correlation. Additionally, drug prediction and molecular docking (binding energy: −8.552 kcal/mol) indicated strong binding between LDHA and CHEMBL2058994. Subsequent 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations affirmed the structural and energetic stability of the LDHA–CHEMBL2058994 complex in silico, suggesting its potential as a candidate for further experimental and pharmacological evaluation in NPC. RT-qPCR validation confirmed significant differential expression for LDHA and PIGR, whereas POSTN exhibited a consistent trend without reaching statistical significance in NPC tissue. This study identified three key ERG candidate genes (LDHA, PIGR, and POSTN) with potential biomarker value. RT-qPCR validation confirmed significant differential expression of LDHA and PIGR, while POSTN showed a consistent upregulation trend in nasopharyngeal carcinoma tissues but did not reach statistical significance, requiring further evaluation in a larger sample cohort.

stories.title: Mechanistic development of a mild palladium-catalyzed C-S/C-H cross-coupling of thioesters with azoles
stories.description: The catalytic C-H acylation of heteroarenes utilizing abundant carboxylic acid derivatives is a highly desirable chemical transformation. However, current procedures require unstable electrophiles, harsh reaction conditions or strong bases, limiting their substrate scope and consequently hampering applications in complex, densely functionalized systems. In this work, we describe the development of a mild palladium-catalyzed, copper-mediated C-H acylation of azoles, using stable thioester electrophiles and a weak base. Previously difficult substrates such as imidazole derivatives, base-sensitive groups and aliphatic electrophiles could be used in good yields. Furthermore, the reaction showed potential for orthogonal cross-coupling, tolerating aryl bromides, chlorides and boronic acid esters. Elementary steps were investigated by H/D-exchange, initial rate experiments and in operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy. In situ generated bimetallic Pd-Cu complexes are proposed to be the catalytically active species, operating via a non-canonical thioester activation pathway in conjunction with a rate-limiting Cu-phosphite-mediated C-H deprotonation. The catalytic C–H acylation of heteroarenes is a key transformation in organic chemistry, although traditional methods often rely on unstable electrophiles and harsh conditions. Here, the authors present a mild palladium-catalyzed, copper-mediated strategy that employs stable thioester electrophiles and a weak base, enabling broad substrate tolerance along with mechanistic insights obtained via H/D exchange, kinetic analyses and in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy.

stories.title: A genome-wide meta-analysis of actinic keratosis identifies 12 novel loci and overlap with keratinocyte carcinoma and pigmentation
stories.description: Actinic keratosis (AK) is a premalignant skin condition caused by chronic ultraviolet (UV) radiation exposure. Previous studies have identified several AK-associated loci, but large-scale genome-wide association (GWA) studies are limited. Here, we show a large GWAS meta-analysis across five cohorts (FinnGen, UK Biobank, Kaiser Permanente Genetic Epidemiology Research on Adult Health and Aging [GERA] cohort, Rotterdam Study, and Million Veteran Program [MVP]), totaling 166,553 AK cases and 1,179,021 controls of European ancestry. Replication is performed in the All of Us (AoU) cohort. We identify 89 genome-wide significant loci, uncovering 12 novel loci involved in epigenetic regulation (TET2), immune signaling (LINC00271, APOLD1, ORMDL3), or other pathways (MIR205HG, ANKRD50). We confirm the role of known pigmentation and keratinocyte carcinoma (KC) genes (IRF4, MC1R, TYR) and find additional independent signals at those loci through conditional analyses. Multivariate conditional analysis adjusting for skin color and KC (both BCC and cSCC) genome-wide summary statistics using the QSkin Study shows that AK genetic susceptibility is largely explained by the genetic architecture of these two traits. This shared architecture is supported by in silico functional analyses. Our findings broaden our understanding of AK pathogenesis and susceptibility to improve risk prediction for AK susceptibility and progression to KC. A genome-wide meta-analysis of over 166,000 actinic keratosis cases identifies 89 loci, including 12 novel, and shows that genetic susceptibility to this premalignant skin lesion is largely shared with pigmentation traits and keratinocyte carcinoma.

stories.description: Apple gives iPhone Duo's chip, cameras and hinge precise figures. Speakers, microphones and haptic feedback are not among them, and here is why.

stories.title: Aluminum on One Apple Page, Titanium on Another
stories.description: Apple's iPhone 18 Pro specs page says aluminum unibody. Apple's own compare tool says titanium frame. Here is what each page actually states.

stories.title: What Apple Publishes, and the Carbon Figure It Has Not
stories.description: Apple Watch Series 12 uses 40 percent recycled material overall, per Apple. Unlike iPhone 18 Pro, Apple has not published a per-model carbon footprint.
